en: When shall I behold for a long time the Lord who is seated upon the king of birds, whose eyes are like lotuses,
whose limbs are embraced by Ramā, who possesses the luster of the sky, who is clad in yellow garments,
and who holds a mace, a conch, a lotus, and the best of weapons?
Surely this pair of my eyes will attain their fruitfulness by going there. || 1 ||
When shall I behold Him seated upon a jeweled throne within the forest of celestial trees at the heart of the Ocean of Milk, His body embraced by the Daughter of the Ocean,
eternally praised by the gods and extolled by the assembly of the best of sages?
I shall gratify the Preceptor of the Gods with hymns containing the words of the Vedas.

When will the Gaṅgā, having abandoned her passion for me—me who am fearless of the ocean of fear, whose body is that of an ascetic, who dwell in mountain caves on the banks of the Ganges, and who constantly cry out, "O Viṣṇu! O best of gods! O Lord of Ramā!"—come to my aid?
Having approached, the lotus-eyed one will speak noble words.

When will that all-pervading Lord, whose feet are to be served by the world of Rasā, dwell forever within the lotus of my heart like a bee in a lotus, having been incessantly summoned through the constant practice of meditation, manifesting as a form of shimmering light like the sun?
It will swiftly remove all the darkness produced by ignorance. || 4 ||

When will my mind— purified by austerity, awakened by the words of the Guru, and made steady and unwavering— having brought silence to itself, dwell for a long time beautifully at the feet of Hari, its hope for worldly enjoyments having ceased from the dense snare of existence?
He shall attain the supreme state, which is as stable as a pillar and removes the fear of worldly existence.
When will my mind— its entire network of senses restrained on all sides,
its retinue of vital breaths completely conquered,
and fixed upon the lotus feet of Hari while chanting the eternal *oṃkāra*— attain [liberation]?
This entire line of hair will repeatedly experience a thrill of joy.
When will it gradually reach a state of relaxation at the end of its momentum, when the body and the flood of the senses have ceased, and the vital breath has stopped?
Ah, when will it constantly speak from above into my lotus-like face again and again?
"Harī shall make his dwelling here; this place is most purifying. || 7 ||

"When shall I cast off this body like a snake sheds its worn-out skin, and—four-armed, with hands bearing the discus, lotus, and conch, clad in yellow garments, dark as a rain cloud—be led by messengers traveling through the sky who bow before me, to the presence of the Lord, the ender of all suffering? (8)
Thus ends the *Abhilāṣāṣṭaka* composed by the venerable Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmananda.
